sources.finding: Dynamic run resumes from scratch and requires idempotent task code.
Worker creates a fresh run generator and returns dependency identities without retaining application state.
Adjacent distributed scheduler persistence proposal, not the explicit task transition contract.
Normal task serialization omits private parameters; checkpoint scheduling explicitly retains complete round-trippable parameters.

original_contribution: Opt-in explicit JSON state transitions with a checksummed durable journal, retained dynamic requirement structure, parameter-preserving native worker scheduling, output completion gates, sequence/epoch continuation fencing, version/identity guards and explicit reset.

public_solution_overlap.assessment: Ordinary output checkpoints and scheduler persistence are adjacent prior art. No full matching protocol found within bounded source/doc/web/issue searches. Expanded GitHub searches were rate limited, so this is not a universal absence claim.

validation.harbor_oracle_nop: Pending parent integration; fresh direct Docker oracle and baseline completed.

horizon.basis: Interacting transition persistence, dependency reconstruction, native worker cache semantics, lock lifecycle, replay receipts, reset/version state and fault recovery; not inferred from lines of code.

limitations: POSIX local filesystems; no distributed or network-filesystem locking guarantees.
External effects before a durable transition commit can repeat; no exactly-once side-effect claim.
Dependency task classes must be importable and their complete parameters must round-trip.
Corrupt journals fail closed and require separate quiescent administrative archival/removal; reset only accepts structurally valid same-identity state.
A failed commit call can already have committed if failure occurs after atomic replacement.

changes: Normalized ordinary nested yielded requirements to DynamicRequirements only within the verifier helper; neither class nor wrapper type is required from the implementation. The instruction explicitly confirms both forms.
Replaced os.open-only monkeypatching with real filesystem permission denial in a separate reader process.

Removed an assertion that a private completion-cache entry must be popped. The test still requires the missing child to be returned for scheduling and the real workflow to finish; the contract permits bypassing stale cached completion.
No golden source changed. A representative alternate implementation yields ordinary nested structures and integrates them with native worker scheduling, including private parameters.
